semantics: dateutil tests/test_rrule.py, extracted statically with Python's ast module (never executed). Python API cases rrule(FREQ, dtstart=..., **kwargs) were mapped to RRULE text (freq->FREQ, interval, count, until (naive datetime -> floating YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS; date -> YYYYMMDD; UTC-aware -> ...Z), wkst, bysetpos, bymonth, bymonthday, byyearday, byweekno, byweekday (MO..SU; MO(+1)/TU(-1) -> 1MO/-1TU; ints 0..6 = MO..SU), byhour, byminute, bysecond, byeaster -> BYEASTER=n with extensions ["BYEASTER"]); rrulestr(...) cases keep the source's RRULE/EXRULE text verbatim (minus the 'RRULE:' prefix) and its DTSTART/RDATE/EXDATE values; rruleset() cases map .rrule/.exrule/.rdate/.exdate calls (all member rules must share one dtstart). dateutil only yields instances generated by the rules (plus RDATEs): DTSTART is NOT added unless it matches the rule, and COUNT does not count a non-matching DTSTART, so include_dtstart=false - except rrulestr(..., compatible=True), which adds DTSTART as an RDATE (include_dtstart=true). dateutil fills unspecified BYxxx parts from DTSTART exactly like RFC 5545. Unlike RFC 5545 it accepts rule-part combinations that RFC 5545 forbids (e.g. BYWEEKNO/BYYEARDAY with MONTHLY/WEEKLY/DAILY..., BYMONTHDAY with WEEKLY, BYDAY ordinals with non-MONTHLY/YEARLY freq, where the ordinal is ignored); those cases carry NONSTANDARD:* markers in 'extensions'. Naive datetimes are floating; tzinfo=tz.gettz(NAME) gives 'tzid' (wall-clock values); tz.UTC gives Z. dtstart=date(...) is promoted by dateutil to midnight, so dtstart is written as YYYYMMDDT000000. between: rule.between(after, before, inc) - exclusive unless inc=True; after(dt, inc) -> between.start with limit 1; xafter(dt, count=N, inc) -> between.start with limit N; a slice rule[:N] -> limit N. error=true: the source expects ValueError (assertRaises/pytest.raises) at construction or iteration; some of these are dateutil-specific (e.g. rules whose BYxxx can never match with the given INTERVAL).
